newsitem.title: USA: MCI sets alliance to bring multimedia to rural America.
newsitem.headline: MCI sets alliance to bring multimedia to rural America.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp is forming an alliance with a power company and a local phone company to bring competitive local phone services, Internet and entertainment services to rural America.

Sources close to the deal say MCI is beginning in Northern Iowa, allying with local phone company Long Lines Ltd and the Northern Iowa Power Cooperative (NIPCO) to use a hybrid fiber coaxial cable system to deliver the services to homes.

The news, to be announced formally on Thursday, is another blow to regional Bells which assumed they would keep a strong grip on rural customers long after they are fighting tooth and nail to keep big city customers and business users.
"While the Bells have been guarding the front door MCI has sneaked in the back gate," said one source.
U S West Communications and GTE Corp have local calling regions in Iowa.

First services will be available in the summer using cable modems made either by privately-owned Comm 21 Inc by or Motorola Inc, according to the website of one of the participants, consultancy TeleChoice Inc.
3Com Corp owns a stake in Comm 21.
Other companies involved include Westell Technologies Inc, Internet company Pioneer ISP, Northern Telecom Ltd, PairGain Technologies Inc, Performance Telecom and NEC Corp an MCI news advisory said.
None of the companies involved would comment. No figures on MCI's investment were disclosed, nor on exactly how many customers would be served.

Analysts have predicted that competition for local calling services, made possible in the 1996 Telecommunications Act, will materialise only slowly in rural areas where it is expensive to lay new phone lines and residents are spread out.
But power companies, which have fiberoptic cables alongside their powerlines into communities, could change that and enter a profitable new business, too.

Industry studies say rural residents could be amongst the heaviest potential users of Internet commerce just as they were mail order pioneers, because many are tens of miles away from the nearest big city stores.
Last month AT&T Corp announced a fast wireless system it was developing to provide local and long distance calling, and high speed Internet access to some local areas.
